newsitem.title: MOLDOVA: Lucinschi looks set to become Moldova president.
newsitem.headline: Lucinschi looks set to become Moldova president.

text.p: Leftist challenger Petru Lucinschi was heading for victory over Moldovan President Mircea Snegur on Monday after more than three-quarters of the vote had been counted in the presidential election run-off.

After a bitter campaign in the former Soviet republic that pitted the president against the government, parliament chairman Lucinschi led by more than six points with 76 percent of the ballot counted.

Pro-Snegur students gathered in front of the electoral commission in the centre of the capital Chisinau, vowing to protest if the president lost. But they numbered only about a hundred and dispersed by the early hours of the morning.

Electoral officials said Lucinschi, who is backed by communists but presents himself as a social democrat, had 53.14 percent of the vote. Snegur, who has led Moldova since independence from Moscow in 1991, had 46.86 percent .

No voting figures were available for Chisinau where Lucinschi had been expected to do well among Moldova's mainly urban one-third Russian-speaking minority, who are suspicious of Snegur's calls for closer ties with the majority's ethnic kin in Romania.
Nationwide turnout was 69 percent, up on the 67 percent first round total on November 17.
